messages:
megan: FYI tenant 'nexis' reporting 403s when trying to create model inference jobs. billing page OK but model API returns permission error. anyone seen this after the role schema changes yesterday?

samir: can you paste the error/trace and the tenant's effective roles?

megan: here's the top of the error from the agent logs:
```
2026-03-19T18:04:12Z ERROR request_id=abc123 auth=denied reason=missing_permission permission=model.use resource=model:open-llama-13b tenant=nexis
```
Also pulled effective bindings (redacted):
```
- principal: user:nexis-admin@example.com
  roles: [tenant-admin, billing-admin]
- principal: service:workflows@redwood
  roles: [model-invoker]
```

elaine: looks like model-level permission is model.use which is in the new "model-invoker" role, but your binding shows model-invoker on a service principal only. did the tenant-admin role lose the model-invoker composite yesterday?

megan: i compared the v2->v3 mapping that ran in prod: the mapping dropped the composite for tenant-admin for tenants that had custom role overrides. example diff:
```diff
- role: tenant-admin -> includes: [org-read, model-invoker]
+ role: tenant-admin -> includes: [org-read]
```

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-8721 created for tenant nexis: "model deploys failing due to missing model.use after role refactor". Escalation level: high.

audit-bot: Detected policy-change event 2026-03-19T03:22:05Z (migration-runner v2.7) affecting 1,142 tenants. Event details: mapping-applied -> mapping_id=map-v3-2026-03-19.

samir: ok two things to check: 1) is KMS grant for model keys still attached for tenant nexis? 2) did the migration inadvertently remove the model-invoker binding from tenant-admin? if (1) fails we can still grant model-invoker to the tenant-admin temporarily to unblock.

megan: KMS looks odd — the model KMS alias is pointing at the wrong key id for this tenant. from the kms audit:
```
alias/redwood/models/nexis -> projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/models/cryptoKeys/models_v1 (expected: models_nexis_v1)
```
So two separate issues: model permission missing and KMS alias mismatch. suspect the mapping script had a faulty key templating substitution for custom tenants.

elaine: we should not change KMS keys manually without sec approval. plan: (A) temporarily re-grant model-invoker to tenant-admin for nexis via role override (expiring 15m), (B) open a follow-up to fix mapping templates and do a safe reapply to correct KMS aliases, (C) run canary tests.

megan: can someone approve (A)? need a short-lived bypass so customer can resume production.

ash: i can approve a 15m exception. Security note: will log and rotate any short-lived keys created. Approving now — please include ticket id SUP-8721 in the action.

samir: executing remediation now:
```bash
rbacctl grant --tenant nexis --role model-invoker --principal user:nexis-admin@example.com --expires-in 15m --reason "SUP-8721 temporary unblock"
```

megan: ran it, and the deploy now moves past auth: creating job succeeded. upstream workflows started.

support-bot: SUP-8721 update: customer notified, access restored.

elaine: next steps: schedule a rollback-proof mapping fix (add tests for kms alias templating), run migration in a dry-run and a small batch, and add an alert when a tenant's kms alias doesn't match expected pattern.

samir: also adding a postmortem board item and will propose a resolver script to auto-detect tenants with missing composites and queue a safe reapply.

megan: can we also add a nightly canary that creates a minimal model job for a small set of tenants? this would have caught the issue earlier.

ash: agree. security will also add a read-only KMS consistency audit that runs daily and alerts on mismatches.

megan: thanks all — closing the immediate loop. will keep SUP-8721 open for the mapping fix + postmortem. :thumbsup:

elaine: noted, tagging eng-runtime and eng-security for the mapping patch and canary plan. :eyes:

samir: good catch. nice cross-team coordination. :party:
